description: Complex left-cluster loading: every historical coil moves; NEW may have large gap, yaw and imperfect target; rolling/partial observations are combined.
All old coils move; NEW is intentionally not touching its neighbor and has +7deg yaw; robot target is offset.
Second NEW while every old coil moves; one historical coil is side-occluded after rolling observation change.
Third NEW has +8deg yaw and a large internal gap; old coils undergo non-rigid settling and one-sided occlusion.
No NEW; the whole cluster settles/rebounds with non-uniform X/Y/Z changes and rolling observation mismatch.
Complex right-cluster loading: mirrored edge growth with large NEW gaps, negative yaw, all-history motion and partial visibility.
Right cluster grows inward; NEW is separated by a large gap and has -7deg yaw while all history moves.
Second inward NEW; old coils move non-uniformly and ID8 is partially hidden on its right side.
Third right-cluster NEW has -8deg yaw and abnormal gap; every existing coil shifts again.
Right cluster settles with small reverse motion; no NEW.
Two edge clusters grow alternately; both clusters move, NEW gaps/yaw vary, partial/occluded history appears, and the middle free region stays semantically normal.
Left cluster extends while both clusters move inward; NEW has a large gap and +6deg yaw.
Right cluster extends; all coils move, one left-cluster coil is side-occluded, NEW has -7deg yaw.
Two NEW coils are placed simultaneously, one on each cluster; both have yaw and unequal gaps; all history moves.
No birth; both clusters move and historical ID7 becomes fully occluded while its semantic slot remains occupied.
ID7 returns partially; both clusters settle and the large middle region is still a valid free region, not an abnormal gap.

Adversarial same-geometry sequence: all objects share one prototype, entire cluster shifts by more than half a spacing, then a same-spec NEW appears; nearest-neighbor should fail but order semantics must protect identity.
Every coil shifts +0.72m (> half spacing) with identical D/L and heavy rolling observation mismatch; pure nearest-neighbor is intentionally misleading.
A same-spec NEW appears after another large group shift; NEW target is imperfect and geometry cannot distinguish identities.
Same-spec cluster continues moving; central ID3 becomes heavily side-occluded, creating a high-risk identity-swap case.
One same-spec historical coil disappears completely while all others remain; semantic bracketing should preserve its ID.
Combined difficult loading: historical occlusion and a far-gap yawed NEW occur in the same frame while every visible old coil moves; then the missing ID returns and loading continues.
ID1 is fully occluded while a -8deg NEW appears far from ID3; all historical positions move simultaneously.
Previously hidden ID1 returns partially while all objects continue non-uniform motion and rolling observation changes.
Loading continues with another yawed NEW while ID2 is partially side-occluded and every historical coil moves.
All IDs are visible again after settling; identity must remain unchanged across the earlier NEW+OCCLUDED ambiguity.
Full first layer with progressive second-layer loading. New upper coils have yaw and target error; first-layer coils move slightly and visibility degrades/recovers without layer changes.
First L2 NEW has +7deg yaw; all L1 coils shift slightly and one lower coil becomes partially visible.
Second L2 NEW arrives with -6deg yaw; existing upper/lower coils move and lower ID3 is more strongly obscured.
Third upper NEW while lower ID4 becomes fully occluded; layer identity and slot order must be retained.
No birth; upper coils move/yaw and lower ID4 returns partially.
Fourth L2 NEW has -7deg yaw; lower and upper histories continue small non-rigid motion.
Multi-birth two-side loading: two NEW coils may arrive simultaneously, both with yaw/large gaps, while all old coils move and later one history becomes occluded.
Two simultaneous NEW coils, both strongly yawed and separated from current cluster boundaries; all old coils move.
Two more simultaneous births while prior NEWs roll/shift and an existing coil becomes one-side partial.
No birth; both clusters continue moving and right-cluster ID8 becomes fully occluded.
Occluded ID8 returns partially; cluster identities must remain stable after simultaneous births.
Robot-hint tolerance and large-motion stress: NEW actual positions differ substantially from approximate targets; all histories can shift close to ROI limits with Y/Z drift and yaw.
All old coils move 0.2-0.45m with Y/Z drift; NEW is +8deg yaw, has 0.45m gap, and robot target is ~0.4m offset.
Entire cluster shifts ~0.55-0.65m; second NEW has -7deg yaw and target error in the opposite direction; one old coil is partial.
No birth; the complete cluster shifts +1.05m in one snapshot, intentionally making absolute nearest-neighbor misleading while staying inside configured motion ROI.
Cluster rebounds after the large translation; tests absence of a strict velocity-direction assumption.
Heavy visibility stress without removal: multiple old coils move, become side-partial or fully occluded, then recover; a yawed NEW is inserted during recovery.
Two historical coils are partially visible on different sides while all six objects move and roll.
ID2 is fully occluded while ID4 is partially visible; no old coil is removed and all others continue moving.
Previously occluded ID2 returns partially while a +7deg NEW is inserted with a nonzero gap; all existing coils move.
All objects visible again after the visibility lifecycle; permanent IDs must be unchanged.
Non-monotonic settling sequence: historical coils move in X/Y, change yaw, reverse direction, then receive a far-gap NEW. This tests that tracking is not a one-direction velocity model.
Every historical coil moves forward by a different amount with alternating Y drift and yaw.
The cluster reverses direction after settling; rolling observation changes remain, so a constant-velocity prior would be unsafe.
After a direction reversal, a -8deg NEW is placed with a 0.55m gap while one old coil is partially hidden.
Final settling frame after reverse motion and NEW birth.
